opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin is only for the owning role (Engineer). As a full-time employee, max is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Requested admin on Source Code, so grant max read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin on Source Code. The Security note (looked up employment type and security training in its own database) shows E041 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are never admin and write requires advanced security training, so the maximum allowable level is read. Admin is above the maximum, so I grant the maximum: read. (Note: the HR note lists E041 as full-time and recommends write; due to the conflicting employment-type records, I apply the more restrictive, verifiable security determination.)
